newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end higher for sixth straight session.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end higher for sixth straight session.

text.p: A rally in the Seoul stock market showed no sign of taking a rest as across-the-board buying sent the index closing higher for the sixth consecutive session on Friday, brokers said.
The composite stock index shrugged off intra-day profit-taking to close up 3.22 points to a provisional 833.43. Gainers led losers by 626 to 289 with 203 going limit up.
"There are many favourable factors surrounding the market," said Kim Duck-sun, a broker at Hyundai Securities.
Choi Bum, trader at C.S. First Boston, said: "Hope of an interest rate cut will push the market to the 850 level."
Brokers said investors welcomed the government's desire to help boost the ailing economy by improving the global competitivenss of local firms and by lowering interest rates.
"Investors believed the economy has hit the bottom and the worst has gone," Kim said.

The pay-back of heavy margin loans during the recent rally was an another factor to help clear off clouds from the market and keep the market rising. Concerns over the overhang of margin calls have pressured the market in the past weeks.
Anticipation of new cash inflows from a stock savings scheme also contributed to backing the recent rally.

Funds from savings on tax benefits, which the finance ministry had offered to workers willing to put their money in the stock market, will begin trading from next Monday. The ministry earlier estimated about two trillion own would flow into the market by the plan.
Low-priced large-cap shares, which had underperformed the market, and some individual shares continued to attract strong buying interest, brokers said.
Kukje went limit up, gaining 350 won to 6,250. It was the most actively traded stock with 670,970 shares changing hands. Shin Ho Paper also hit upper limit of 390 won to 7,050.
